judgments.title: NG CHEE GONG & ors v CHAI WENG SING & ors
judgments.catchwords: Having considered the pleadings, the authorities and the submissions, I am satisfied that the claim against the 8th Defendant, Public Bank Berhad (“PBB”), presents a plain and obvious case for striking out. The statement of claim does not articulate any material facts capable of sustaining a cause of action in conspiracy, fraud or forgery, or under the Moneylenders Act. The allegations advanced against PBB are broad, unparticularised and unsupported by pleaded acts, knowledge or statutory triggers. They fall far short of the particularity required for serious accusations of fraud and conspiracy, and do not disclose any coherent legal basis upon which PBB could be held liable. The continued joinder of PBB in these proceedings would prejudice and embarrass the fair trial of the action. The pleading seeks to attach liability by association rather than by pleading the constituent elements of any tort or statutory wrong. This is precisely the type of misuse of the court’s process contemplated by Order 18 rule 19(1)(a), (b), (c) and (d) of the Rules of Court 2012. Accordingly, the 8th Defendant’s application is allowed. The Plaintiffs’ claim against Public Bank Berhad is struck out in its entirety pursuant to Order 18 rule 19(1)(a), (b), (c) and (d) of the Rules of Court 2012. Costs of this application and of the action as against the 8th Defendant are awarded to Public Bank Berhad, fixed in the sum of RM5,000.00. I hereby order so.

judgments.title: NG CHEE GONG & ors v CHAI WENG SING & ors
judgments.catchwords: Having examined the entirety of the cause papers, affidavits, submissions and the procedural history placed before the Court, the following conclusions emerge with clarity and without ambiguity: • First, the Statement of Claim does not disclose any reasonable cause of action against D2. The pleadings contain no material facts connecting her to the alleged wrongdoing. • Second, the claim against D2 is frivolous, vexatious, and an abuse of process, resting solely on marital association and unsupported inference. • Third, the Lot 31703 dispute has already been tried, appealed, settled, and fully performed. The doctrines of res judicata, issue estoppel, and cause of action estoppel therefore apply with full force. • Fourth, the present writ constitutes a collateral attack on concluded judicial decisions and a perfected Consent Order. This Court cannot be invited to sit in review over matters already adjudicated by courts of competent jurisdiction. • Fifth, the Plaintiffs have pleaded no newly discovered fraud capable of impeaching the Consent Order. The allegations relied upon are the same matters already known and raised before settlement. Taken together, these findings reveal a claim that seeks to reopen what the law has already closed, to relitigate what has already been resolved, and to disturb the finality that the judicial process has already conferred. The Court cannot permit such an attempt. The integrity of final judgments, the sanctity of settlement, and the orderly administration of justice demand that this action, as against D2, must come to an end. The claim against D2 is unsustainable in law and must be struck out. Order Of The Court Enclosure 29 is allowed. The Plaintiffs’ Writ and Statement of Claim dated 29.12.2025 are struck out as against the 2nd Defendant. Costs of RM5,000.00 are awarded to D2 to be paid by the Plaintiffs.

judgments.catchwords: CRIMINAL APPEAL — Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 — Possession of dangerous drugs — Section 12(2) — Burden of proof — Prosecution required to prove possession beyond reasonable doubt — Accused not required to prove innocence — Drugs found in camouflage bag behind bedroom door — Appellant denying possession, custody and knowledge — Bedroom unlocked and accessible to another person — Material discrepancies in Prosecution evidence — Failure to call material witness — Competing reasonable inferences — Whether reasonable doubt raised as to Appellant’s possession and knowledge — Whether conviction unsafe — Appeal allowed — Conviction and sentence set aside — Appellant acquitted and discharged. EVIDENCE — Material discrepancies and contradictions — Conflicting evidence of Prosecution witnesses as to timing of raid and presence and arrest of another person — Failure to call or offer material witness to Defence — Other persons having possible access to bedroom where drugs were found — Whether the discrepancies materially affected reliability of Prosecution’s case and whether adverse inference ought to be drawn under Section 114(g) of the Evidence Act 1950. Held, allowing the Appellant’s appeal: The appeal concerned the Appellant’s conviction for possession of dangerous drugs under the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952. The Prosecution’s case relied principally on drugs discovered in a camouflage bag behind the Appellant’s bedroom door. The Appellant denied possession, custody and knowledge, maintaining that another person had access to the unlocked bedroom. The appeal focused on material contradictions in the Prosecution’s evidence concerning the raid, another person’s presence and arrest, and the chronology of events. The Prosecution also failed to call or offer a material witness to the Appellant. The cumulative effect of these matters raised reasonable doubt as to possession and rendered the conviction unsafe.

Sekatan perjalanan dikeluarkan selaras dengan kuasa Responden di bawah seksyen 49 Akta 762. Isu utama adalah berkenaan asas pengeluaran sekatan perjalanan yaang diasaskan semata-mata atas dasar terdapatnya cukai tunggakan oleh Syarikat, yang mana Pemohon-Pemohon adalah Pengarah Syarikat. Peruntukan sek 49 Akta 762 tidak boleh terpakai secara automatik dengan hanya bersandarkan kepada kewujudan cukai tertunggak. Perlu wujud bukti atau keterangan lain bagi menyokong bahawa Pemohon-Pemohon merupakan flight risk barulah sekatan perjalanan di bawah sek 49 Akta 762 boleh dikeluarkan.

judgments.catchwords: Undang-undang Perlembagaan - Perlembagaan Persekutuan - Keabsahan Seksyen 12 Akta Senjatapi (Penalti Lebih Berat) 1971 (“FIPA”) - Sama ada Parlimen mempunyai kuasa untuk menggubal undang-undang bagi menghalang Mahkamah daripada menjalankan budi bicara kehakiman untuk membenarkan ikat jamin - Doktrin pengasingan kuasa - Sama ada doktrin pengasingan kuasa merupakan sebahagian daripada asas Perlembagaan - Sama ada terdapat asas bagi menjalankan budi bicara kehakiman berhubung dengan ikat jamin bagi orang yang didakwa atas kesalahan berkaitan senjata api menurut Seksyen 12 FIPA - Hak kesamarataan di sisi undang-undang - Sama ada Seksyen 12 FIPA bertentangan dengan prinsip kesamarataan yang termaktub dalam Perkara 8 Perlembagaan Persekutuan - Maksim “generalia specialibus non derogant” - Sama ada peruntukan berhubung larangan ikat jamin di bawah Seksyen 12 FIPA dimaksudkan untuk mengatasi peruntukan ikat jamin yang bersifat lebih umum menurut Seksyen 388 Kanun Tatacara Jenayah.

judgments.catchwords: Duty of care- deceased was never a patient to the First Respondent, there was no duty owed towards the deceased- not reasonably foreseeable that the First Respondent’s act or omission when performing the autopsy would cause the Appellant to suffer loss- The autopsy also was not conducted by the First Respondent at the request of the Appellant.
